notes:
LOCATION: The whole list is on n92.jpg (printed page 85). n90 (p. 83) and n91 (p. 84) carry the end of the report text and the signatures of A. G. More and R. M. Barrington. n93 (p. 86) begins 'General Remarks of Light-Keepers'. The heading is 'LIST OF LIGHT-STATIONS.' (small caps). The key is printed below the table: 'o = No reply.', 'x = Schedule returned partly or wholly filled.', '* = No schedule sent to this station.'

ROW COUNT: 40 rows are printed, not 42. The numbers run 1–8, 5.*, 8.*, 10–34, 36–40. Nos. 9 and 35 are not in the print at all, so the OCR dropped nothing. The gap is the printer's (or the committee's), possibly Wicklow Head and Loop Head, but that is only a guess. The starred numbers are printed '5.*' and '8.*', with the star after the full stop. I give them as '5*' and '8*' in number and keep '5.*' and '8.*' in printed.

COLUMNS AND FIELD CONVENTIONS: The column heads are Spring, Autumn, 'Miles from shore.' and 'Names of Observers.'
- marks: the Spring mark, then the Autumn mark (o / x / *), e.g. 'o x'.
- other: the 'Miles from shore' figure exactly as printed: a number, '½', or an en-dash '–' where none is given.
- type: the only type printed is 'Lt.-ship' (rows 5*, 6, 7, 8, 8*, 10). No row is marked L.H.
- character: this list gives no light characters, so every character is null.
- coast: the list has no coast sub-headings, so coast is null throughout. Every row belongs to the 'Irish Coast' section (page running head 'IRISH COAST.').
- printed: I left out the dot leaders between name and marks. The dots after 'do.' in rows 6, 7 and 8* are leaders. A brace '{' groups two observer names onto one row in rows 2, 10, 14, 21, 23 and 27. In printed I show it as '{' before the names.
- keepers: each brace joins two people with full names and 'and', so I split them into two entries. The full stop that ends each observer entry is dropped from keepers but kept in printed.

NAMING CHOICES (check before merging):
- 'Old Head, Kinsale, Cork': I put name 'Old Head' and place 'Kinsale, Cork'. The General Remarks call the station 'Old Head, Kinsale', so you may prefer that as the name.
- 'Eagle Island, E.', 'Eagle Island, W.', 'Slyne Head, N.', 'Slyne Head, S.', 'Arran Island, N.' and 'Arran Island, S.': the compass letter is kept in the name and the county goes in place.
- 'Oyster Island, N. Sligo': place is given as printed, 'N. Sligo'.
- 'Barrels Rock' and 'Tuskar Rock' have place 'do.' (= Wexford). 'Arklow North' has 'do.' (= Wicklow).

SPELLINGS COPIED AS PRINTED: Coningbeg, Barrels Rock, Howth Baily (i.e. Baily), Innishtrahull, Arranmore, Rathlin O’Birne (with a curly apostrophe), Arran Island (Aran), Valentia, Thomas Sweeny, Michael Cunniam, John Pinston. The last two are clearly printed but are unusual surnames, worth checking against other years. Tuskar Rock is printed as a 'Lt.-ship', though it was a rock lighthouse; this may be a slip in the print.

WHERE THE OCR IS WRONG (the image is clear in each case):
- Row 2 has Autumn 'x', not '*'. Its keepers are John Whelan and John Kelly; both names are confirmed by the Galley Head remarks on p. 86.
- Row 13 has '3' and 'John Walsh'.
- Rows 30 and 31 have miles '3', not '8'. In this typeface 3 is often read as 8 by the OCR, which also gives '18.' for 13 and '84.' for 34.
- Row 36 has miles '½' (OCR '3}').
- The row the OCR shows as '#0.' is 38 Valentia, and 'mee ewes, Remy.' is 39 Skelligs, Kerry.

OTHER POINTS:
- Some observers appear at more than one station. Joseph Hill is named at 21 Rathlin O’Birne and 23 Oyster Island. John Young is named at 23 Oyster Island and 27 Blackrock. Patrick Keenan is named at 14 Maidens and 24 Broadhaven, possibly two different men.
- Stations with no observer named: 4 Mine Head, 11 Howth Baily, 31 Slyne Head S., 36 Samphire Island. Each is marked 'o' (no reply) or '*' (no schedule sent) in at least one season.
- Howth Baily is 'o o', no reply in either season.
